persons.name: Raṅganātha
persons.evidence: idaṃ pustakaṃ marāṭhe ity upanāmakasya śrīraṃganāthadīkṣitasya

notes: The era is Śaka: the colophon says 'śake 1758', and 1758 + 78 = 1836 CE. The year name Durmukha agrees: in the 60-year cycle it is 1836/37 CE (Śaka 1758). Jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa ekādaśī would then fall around June 1836. The catalogue's 'SAM 1758' has the right number but a vague era label. Both persons are identified by Maharashtrian surnames (upanāma: Kelakara = Kelkar, Marāṭhe), which points to a Marathi brahmin setting in Kāśī. The colophon only says the book belongs to Raṅganātha Dīkṣita. That it was written for him is an inference, not stated. 'śrīgaṃgāviśveśvara (!) prasanno stu' is an invocation of deities, not a person.
